title: Welsh Cakes
subtitle: Griddle-cooked spiced fruit cakes from Wales
excerpt: Small round cakes cooked on a dry griddle or heavy frying pan, spiced with mixed spice and packed with currants. Best eaten warm straight from the pan with a dusting of caster sugar.
sourceNotes: S. Minwel Tibbott, Welsh Fare: A Selection of Traditional Recipes (1976), National Museum of Wales. Welsh cakes (picau ar y maen) have been made in Wales since at least the mid-nineteenth century, traditionally cooked on a bakestone over an open fire. Elias Owen, Welsh Folklore (1888) notes bakestone cooking as widespread in Welsh farmhouses.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooled cakes in a single layer, then transfer to a bag. Defrost at room temperature for 30 minutes. Warm briefly in a dry pan before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily. The dough keeps wrapped in the fridge for up to 2 days.

content.text: Welsh cakes are griddle-cooked rounds of spiced dough with currants: compact, slightly crumbly, and nowhere near as sweet as a biscuit or as soft as a scone. They cook on a dry, ungreased heavy pan over medium heat and need no oven. The whole batch is done in 20 minutes and they are best eaten warm, dusted with caster sugar.

items.prepNote: if needed to bring the dough together

content.text: Put {{self-raising-flour}} of self-raising flour into a large bowl. Add {{salted-butter}} of cold cubed butter and rub in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Stir in {{caster-sugar}} of caster sugar, {{currants}} of currants, and {{mixed-spice}} of mixed spice.
Add {{eggs}} beaten egg and mix until the dough comes together. It should be firm, not sticky. If it is too dry, add {{whole-milk}} of milk a teaspoon at a time.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough to about 7 mm thick. Cut into rounds with a 6 cm cutter. Gather the scraps, re-roll, and cut again.

Heat a heavy frying pan or cast-iron griddle over medium-low heat. Do not grease it. Cook the cakes in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. They should not be dark or singed on the outside but still raw inside: adjust the heat down if they colour too fast.
Dust hot cakes with caster sugar and eat warm.

rows.symptom: Cakes are dark outside but doughy inside
rows.cause: Heat too high so the outside cooks faster than the inside
rows.fix: Lower the heat to medium-low and extend the cooking time. Welsh cakes need a slow, even heat.

rows.cause: Not enough egg or milk to bind, or moved before they had time to set
rows.fix: Add a splash more milk to the dough. Do not flip until the underside is properly set and golden.

rows.symptom: Dough is sticky and hard to roll
rows.cause: Too much liquid or butter not rubbed in finely enough
rows.fix: Wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Dust the surface generously with flour.
Medium-low heat throughout. If currants on the surface are burning before the centres cook through, reduce the heat further.

content.text: Welsh cakes, known in Welsh as picau ar y maen (cakes on the stone), have been made on a flat bakestone over the hearth in Welsh farmhouses since at least the nineteenth century. They are the single most emblematic food item associated with Wales and are sold at markets, railway stations, and roadside stalls throughout the country. Cardiff Market and Swansea Market both have vendors who have sold them continuously for decades. They are not a special-occasion food: they are an everyday snack, made in large batches and eaten over several days.
